title: Embed cohort canary + scale profiling: samplers, metrics, and regression gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a production-ready canary and profiling harness for embedding/rerank endpoints that emphasizes cohort-level stability and scale behavior. Deliverables: cohort samplers (temporal + skewed tail), offline quality metrics, throughput/latency profiling at varying batch sizes, and automated regression gates for CI/CD.
background: Current nightly embedding checks focus on average similarity stats and anchor sets. We still see intermittent regressions affecting small but important cohorts (multi-lingual queries, long-doc anchors) and occasional tail-latency amplification under high burst load. This ticket centralizes a more robust, reproducible harness that matches production routing and KV-cache warmup patterns.
goals: Create configurable cohort samplers (time-window holdouts, user-segment skew, heavy-hitter downsampling)
Compute robust offline metrics: cohort-based recall@k, pairwise stability, calibration drift, and median/95/99 token-latency for rerank flows
Simulate production scale: request arrival bursts, continuous batching behavior, and KV-cache cold vs warmed trajectories
Integrate regression gates into PR checks and nightly pipelines with alerting to SRE & embeddings owners
approach: Data: extract representative logs from s3://redwood-ops/embeddings/2026/ — build temporal holdouts (T-7d, T-30d) and segment slices (lang, doc-length, tenant-tier)
Sampler: implement a 'cohort-sampler' service in the eval runner that can generate replay workloads preserving inter-arrival times or emit burst patterns for scale tests
Metrics: compute per-cohort pairwise rank-correlation (Spearman), normalized recall@k, calibration slope, and delta-cost/token under quantized embeddings
Load: use existing perf harness infra (ENG-15833) to drive synthetic traffic against dedicated staging clusters; run experiments with 1-256 concurrency and batch windows 5-100ms
Gates: add threshold checks that fail CI if cohort recall drops >3% absolute or 95p latency increases >20% compared to baseline run
acceptance_criteria: Cohort sampler implementation merged and documented (README + example config)
Nightly pipeline runs on temporal holdouts and posts structured reports to the embeddings dashboard with cohort-level metrics
Load profiles (cold, warm, burst) run reproducibly and results stored in perf-bench S3 path
Automated PR gate that runs a cheap cohort smoke and rejects if critical cohort recall regresses beyond threshold
Runbook entry for SRE/owners describing how to interpret cohort signals and trigger rollback or mitigation
milestones: M2: Metric adapters + cohort dashboard integration — 2026-03-15
M3: Load profiles + perf storage & baselining — 2026-03-22
implementation_notes: Prefer streaming computation for pairwise metrics to avoid O(n^2) memory blowups; use reservoir sampling and blockwise comparisons
KV-cache warmup is critical: replay sequences should include realistic context growth patterns to exercise cache eviction heuristics
When measuring cost/token delta for quantized variants, normalize for sequence length and batching behavior
Use existing SDK hooks to switch models in-situ for canary vs baseline comparisons (avoid full redeploys)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: holdout data may leak PII. Mitigation: run a PII scrub stage using redwood-dataprotection scripts before storing test sets
Risk: running high-concurrency profiles can impact shared staging clusters. Mitigation: schedule during maintenance window and provide safe-rate caps
Risk: noisy metrics due to upstream tokenization differences across model variants. Mitigation: canonicalize tokenization in runner and include tokenization delta in reports
notes: Parallel work: align with PM roadmap for reranker A/B experiments (PM-1802)
Coordinate with privacy team for data retention window — current default is 30 days for test artifacts
Consider adding a light-weight on-device embed comparator to speed up per-PR checks if CI time becomes the bottleneck
